clue.text: Make a song about dank air that circulates in Austria

indicators.note: about means going round, so the song wraps around the cold air

parts.note: to make a song is to sing
dank, cold air is a chill

explanation.surface: Someone sings about the damp air drifting around Austria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts CHILL inside SING. 'Circulates' looks like a description of the air but belongs to the definition: currency circulates.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the national currency of Austria before the euro, and money is said to circulate.

clue.text: A ring with a line attached to it?

parts.note: a line or string is a cord
something attached is on, as in 'with the lid on'

explanation.surface: A ring with a cord tied to it, like a key fob.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordon is a ring of police or troops surrounding an area.

clue.text: They have to dispose of their frozen assets to survive

definitions.text: They have to dispose of their frozen assets to survive

parts.words: They have to dispose of their frozen assets to survive
parts.note: frozen assets sounds like financial jargon for locked funds, but here it is literal ice, which sellers of ice must sell before it melts

explanation.surface: Investors must liquidate their frozen holdings to stay afloat.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice-sellers of old delivered blocks of ice and had to sell their stock before it melted away.

clue.text: In store? Well, no

definitions.meaning: put away or stored for later use
not well, that is ill and confined to bed

explanation.definitionFit: Laid up means stored away out of use, and also confined to bed through illness.

clue.text: Short of a length?

parts.note: reads like cricket jargon for a ball pitched short, but means simply a short distance

explanation.surface: A bowler's delivery falls short of a good length.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a 'length' is where a bowler pitches the ball; here 'short of a length' is read literally as only a small span.
explanation.definitionFit: Something short in length covers only a small span, close at hand.

clue.text: Those who are privileged to be in the royal train

definitions.text: Those who are privileged to be in the royal train

parts.words: Those who are privileged to be in the royal train
parts.note: a train here is a retinue of followers, not a railway carriage carrying royalty

explanation.surface: Selected passengers ride the royal railway carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue of attendants following an important person, as a train of followers does.

clue.text: Lucky at coming into a large sum of money

indicators.note: coming into says one piece enters the other, so the small word sits inside

parts.note: a fortune is a large sum of money
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is lucky to inherit a large sum of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Being blessed with good fortune is being lucky.

clue.text: Starts a new life?

parts.note: sounds like someone beginning afresh, but means bringing a new life into being

explanation.surface: Someone moves away to begin again.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring into being or beget, as parents do with offspring.

clue.text: Rent-free?

parts.note: rent here is a rip or tear, not payment for housing, so free of rips

explanation.surface: A lodging with nothing to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Intact fabric with no tears or rips in it.

clue.text: Terse instructions to counsel

parts.note: brief means terse, and the instructions a solicitor gives a barrister are also called briefs

explanation.surface: Curt orders handed to a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a solicitor instructs a barrister (counsel) with a document called a brief.
explanation.definitionFit: Short instruction sessions, and the papers by which counsel is engaged.

clue.text: Dutch courage!

parts.note: Dutch courage is bravery from drink, which comes from this container; the word is also British slang for nerve

explanation.surface: Drinking for confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' is British slang for courage, and Dutch courage comes out of one.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve in British slang, and the vessel that alcoholic confidence is poured from.

clue.text: Enemy agent with tortuous clues for small particles of matter

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted by the enemy

indicators.note: tortuous means twisted, so the letters of the next word are twisted round

explanation.surface: A spy with twisted clues is hunting for tiny particles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tortuous' rearranges CLUES into CULES, following MOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the smallest units of a chemical compound, tiny bits of matter.

clue.text: Pressed on amid dire trouble

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one word goes inside the other
trouble suggests stirring up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone pressed on despite dire trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' turns DIRE into IRED, and 'amid' puts ON inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes smoothed with a hot iron have been pressed.

clue.text: Politically, it's stirring stuff!

parts.note: stirring means both rousing and physically shaking up, and in politics it means campaigning unrest

explanation.surface: A political speech that rouses the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Political campaigning for change, and also the act of shaking or stirring.

clue.text: Fail to appreciate the speed of a submerged submarine?

definitions.text: Fail to appreciate the speed of a submerged submarine?

parts.words: Fail to appreciate the speed of a submerged submarine?
parts.note: read playfully, the pace of a submarine below the surface is its rate under water

explanation.surface: Someone misjudges how fast a submarine travels underwater.
explanation.definitionFit: To value something too low is to fail to appreciate it properly.

clue.text: A beggar can put in to repair it

parts.note: to repair is to mend

indicators.note: put in says the small word goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A beggar could put his tin to use repairing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' sets CAN inside IT, giving ICANT, after MEND.
explanation.definitionFit: A mendicant is someone who lives by begging, like a friar of a begging order.

clue.text: 18's past form

parts.note: the past tense of the verb at 18 down, to dine

explanation.surface: A grammar note on a verb's past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: The simple past tense of the verb meaning to dine.

clue.text: A tree-snake with a dangerous bite

definitions.meaning: an old name for the aspen, a poplar
a venomous viper, such as the one that killed Cleopatra

explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for the aspen poplar, and also a small venomous Egyptian viper.

clue.text: Dine in style at a restaurant

indicators.note: in says the letters are held inside the following words

explanation.surface: Dining in style at a smart restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: To dine is to take a meal, to consume food.

clue.text: When Jack kissed her he was given a flogging

definitions.text: When Jack kissed her he was given a flogging

parts.words: When Jack kissed her he was given a flogging
parts.note: Jack is a sailor, and to kiss this lady was naval slang for being tied over a cannon and flogged

explanation.surface: A sailor kisses a girl and is punished for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack (Jack tar) is a sailor; old navy floggings were given with the victim lashed over a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: In old Royal Navy slang, the cannon over which a sailor was bent for punishment.

clue.text: A fruit-stone that's mine

definitions.meaning: the hard seed inside a cherry or peach, in American usage

explanation.definitionFit: American English calls a fruit's stone this, and a colliery is also called this.

clue.text: Fashionable conclusion to test out

indicators.note: out here means spread round the outside, so test encloses the ending

parts.note: to test is to try
a conclusion is an end

explanation.surface: A fashionable conclusion to try out.
explanation.definitionFit: Up to date and stylish is a synonym for in fashion.

clue.text: Clasp a bony part of the leg

definitions.meaning: an ancient Roman brooch or pin
the outer, thinner bone of the lower leg

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for a brooch pin, and also the slender calf bone beside the shin.

clue.text: Sun-girt porker of great importance in feudal Japan

definitions.text: of great importance in feudal Japan
definitions.note: an adjectival phrase standing for a noun: one who was of great importance

indicators.note: girt means encircled, so the sun goes round the pig

parts.note: taken as written
a porker is a pig or hog

explanation.surface: A pig ringed by sunlight was revered in old Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: The hereditary military dictator who held real power in feudal Japan.

clue.text: A standard author not translated into French?

parts.note: to author a work is to pen it
the French word for no or not is non

explanation.surface: A standard writer left untranslated into French.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow flag carried on a lance, a kind of banner or standard.

clue.text: Alchemist transformed into a heavenly prince

indicators.note: transformed suggests changed shape, so the letters are rearranged, fitting an alchemist's trade

explanation.surface: An alchemist turns himself into an archangel.
explanation.definitionFit: The archangel, named in Daniel as a great prince and leader of the heavenly host.

clue.text: Vehicle taken back into the northernmost part of Greece

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: taken back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A car is driven back into northern Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken back' turns CAR into RAC, which goes 'into' THE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient region straddling the north-eastern tip of Greece, bordering Turkey and Bulgaria.

clue.text: Rebel gunners are deployed in it

indicators.note: deployed means arranged in position, so the letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: Rebel gunners are sent into action.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone rising in revolt against authority is an insurgent.

clue.text: A hydrocarbon that can make one act

indicators.note: can make says the letters may be made into something new

explanation.surface: A fuel that can make someone act.
explanation.definitionFit: A paraffin compound of eight carbon atoms, found in petrol.

clue.text: Getting one's own back

parts.note: sounds like taking revenge, but means literally recovering what is yours

explanation.surface: Taking revenge on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Recovering something once lost, such as a title or possession.
